results.title: CMS Transmittal 1875 - Consultation service codes no longer recognized for Medicare payment
results.text:
# Medicare consultation code elimination, January 1, 2010

## Policy change

Effective January 1, 2010, Medicare stopped recognizing consultation service codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment under the physician fee schedule. The change was applied budget-neutrally across inpatient and office/outpatient settings, with limited exceptions for telehealth consultation G-codes.

## Rationale

CMS restructured evaluation and management (E/M) payment. The transmittal states that the agency increased the work relative value units (RVUs) for new and established office visits and increased payment for initial hospital and nursing facility visits. These increased values were also carried into practice expense and malpractice calculations and into the E/M component of global surgical codes.

## What to bill instead, by setting

with reassigned billing rights. Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate. ## Documentation

All E/M services must meet existing E/M documentation guidelines. Services should be documented during or immediately after they are provided. Code selection should reflect the actual service content.

## Timeline

The effective date was January 1, 2010, and implementation was January 4, 2010. The transmittal removed all references to consultation codes from Claims Processing Manual Chapter 12, Section 30.6.

final_text:
**Most plausible reason code: CARC 181.** The project's paraphrase reads "The procedure code wasn't valid on the date of service." It maps to the project rule `deprecated_code`.

**Why 181 fits.** The claim bills HCPCS 99241. The CMS Transmittal 1875 document (`cms_r1875cp_consultation_codes`) says that Medicare stopped recognizing consultation codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment effective January 1, 2010. That matches the CARC 181 wording. The policy documents don't give the claim's date of service or say which CARC a payer would attach. So this is an inference, not a confirmed reason. CARCs 11, 16, 18 and 197 have no support in what the tools returned.

**How the score relates.**
- The model gives a denial probability of 0.9283. The validation-set average is 0.1805, so this is 5.14 times the average and 74.8 percentage points above it.
- HCPCS_CD (value 99241) is the main driver. It has a SHAP value of 4.504 log-odds, an odds change of 8934 percent. The tool describes this feature only as "Procedure/service code billed."
- The other features shown each have small SHAP values. The principal diagnosis E785 adds 0.068. The tool lists 153 features not shown.
- The model weighs the procedure code heavily, which is consistent with the deprecated-code rule. It does not identify a reason code, and SHAP values show what the model weighs, not what causes a denial.

The denial label in this project is synthetic. It was engineered from risk rules, so the score reflects that constructed label and not a real payer decision.
